text: The case facts of a business date are published as GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/facts on the rwb-case base, with businessDate, page and size, answering the nine fields of the legacy CaseReportingApi plus the band code, the as-of time, the row count and the reference version.
why: The legacy interface is Java only and no REST operation for it exists in the API Specification v4 or the ownership map, so the operation is composed on the naming rules of Template and Rules R4 and R7.
read: API Specification v4; Ownership Map v1 (P3 rows); Template and Rules R4 and R7.2 s12; legacy RWB-E1-013 section 12
confirm: The P3 API owner confirms the path and the field names before the contract of RWB-P9-E1013-CON is frozen.
impact: The facts read, its fake and the -ITG harness stub use this path until it is confirmed; the values behind it do not change.

text: The measure definitions in force are read from rwb-reporting as a GET on /api/recovery/reporting/v1/measure-definitions with an onDate parameter, under RWB-P9-E1013-CON.
why: The legacy MeasureCatalog.inForce interface is the only evidence of the read and no path for it exists in the API Specification v4, so the call is composed on the naming rules.
read: API Specification v4; Template and Rules R4; legacy RWB-E1-013 section 12
confirm: The P9 API owner confirms the path and the definition fields at the next API revision.
impact: Only the client configuration and the fake change if the path is confirmed differently; no business value depends on it.

text: The age-band list is reference data of rwb-case under the R3 default ruling (parameters and reference data, E1-042 and E1-043, belong to P3 rwb-case), held as a versioned reference table with an effective range per version.
why: Template and Rules R3 assigns parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case, and the legacy story states the bands as a reference list without naming its owner or code.
read: Template and Rules R3 default rulings; legacy RWB-E1-013 BR6; RWB-P3-E1043-APP
confirm: The data steward confirms the list code when the reference catalog is next published.
impact: The band rows and their versions live in rwb_case; consumers read them through the reference-data contract, never as constants.

text: A held facts release is shown as a release state with the business date, the two counts and the case behind the difference, addressed to the data steward, and it carries one new message of rwb-case whose ID and wording are left to the message catalogue.
why: No message is defined for a held release and SCR-44 has no release columns, but the held path is required by REC-01 and by the legacy rule that measures must reconcile.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-013 sections 14 and 15; message catalogue; SCR-44
confirm: The message catalogue owner allocates the ID and the wording before SIT.
impact: The held release is testable without the message ID; only the wording of the alert is open.

text: The legacy story RWB-E1-013 carries status Ready for build and the split is made in this run without a further approval step, so RWB-P3-E1013-APP is issued as Draft (realignment v1) and no additional sign-off is assumed.
why: The realignment overlay allows no human approval stop; a missing approval or status is recorded as an assumption and the story proceeds in Draft.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-013 metadata (Status: Ready for build); AGENTS.md rules 8 and 9; D-RCV-60 overlay
confirm: The epic owner confirms the story at the first realignment review.
impact: The story may be built from this draft; nothing in the content depends on the approval.
